rules: Read the live bank ~/.ai-raccoon read-only only (?mode=ro or PRAGMA query_only=1).
Use a scratch --data-root for every write.
Never bind port 7721; start servers with --port 0 and read the port back.
Never accept a check from a plan; accept only what the running build shows.
Run serve in the background, because it blocks in the foreground.
Open a scratch bank with sqlite3 -readonly only while its server runs (WAL).
Make the scratch data root creatable by the current user.
Prove the installed binary by the +sha in --version, not by the version string.

items.expected-result: Release pack succeeds; install to an isolated tool path, or force-update the global tool when requested; installed --version matches derived.version.
`serve --port 0` binds and reports its port; `serve --restart` on that port cycles the server it finds rather than attaching, and never touches port 7721
add_memory returns a hash for a stored entry; a rejected write returns Stored=false with a reason and no fabricated hash (ADR-0032)
query returns the written entry through hybrid BM25 + vector RRF ranking
get_entry requires one entryType and returns the selected Memory/File/Code entry for a reachable hash; unknown or mismatched types refuse without fallback (2.1.0 changelog, ADR-0035)
a `file#section` query returns that exact chunk within the production result window

add_memory a note made of"The village fete committee met in the church hall to plan stalls, bunting, the tombola and the cake competition." forty-five times, space-joined (ten fit in one chunk since 1.56), then " Invoice reference vk83jq was filed with the parish council." Premise: sqlite shows more than one entries row for the note's path. query {query: "vk83jq", entryType: memory, minRelativeScore: 0} returns the note with an `fts` leg in evidenceByHash, and one of its rows holds `vk83jq` whole (`instr(value,'vk83jq')`). A vector-only hit does not count: the vector leg finds this note on a broken build too. Then write a note holding one whitespace-free term of about 2,500 characters (40 concatenated SHA-256 hex digests); premise: no row holds the whole term; searching the whole term returns that note with an `fts` leg. A build without ADR-0120 returns both notes by the vector leg only, and no row holds vk83jq (ADR-0120)

add_memory a note with sourceFile /notes/minutes.md made of 62 paragraphs separated by blank lines ("Paragraph N of the parish minutes records the treasurer's report on hall repairs, roof slates and the organ fund."), the first opening with "Opening marker zq71". Premise: sqlite shows more than one row for the note's path. query {query: "zq71", entryType: memory, minRelativeScore: 0} returns it with chunkIndex 0, and sqlite gives chunk_index 0 for the row where `instr(value,'zq71') > 0`. A build without ADR-0122 puts the opening at the last index (1 of 2 on 1.56.1) (ADR-0122)

On a fresh scratch bank with no engine set, add_memory four ordinary notes and one containing POISON-7Q, so all five rows are pending. Start `python3 scripts/checklist-poison-embedding-stub.py --port 0 --log stub.log`, then run `model embedding set openai stub-embed <printed base URL> --api-key stub-key` against the scratch server. embed_deferred_entries returns {processed, pending} and does not fail or hang. Later calls return pending 1. `sqlite3 -readonly memory.db "SELECT embed_state, embed_attempts, count(*) FROM entries GROUP BY 1, 2"` shows four rows embedded and the poison row pending at embed_attempts 3. get_store_statistics.pending is 1, and the count of poison lines in stub.log stays the same across three more embed_deferred_entries calls. Negative control: stub.log holds a `poison 5` batch line followed by `ok 1` lines, so the engine refused the batch and answered the single rows. A build without ADR-0119 fails every embed_deferred_entries with ClientResultException, keeps all five rows pending and adds a poison line per call (ADR-0119)
each registered write-path policy rejects what it claims to, the write reports the rejection, and the rejected content is retrievable from the noise store (ADR-0039)
the refuse and annotate tiers behave as ADR-0040 describes; the structural detector is off until `queryguard structural enable` and only ever annotates (ADR-0041)

Copy the live bank with VACUUM INTO (clear its watches) and serve the copy. A query for the first ~7,000 characters of CLAUDE.md, and one for ~7,000 characters of stopwords plus two content words, each return in seconds at vectorWeight 0, and data.warning says keyword matching is capped at the first 64 distinct words, with no clause saying it still sees the query in full. On a fresh bank with vectorWeight 0 and minRelativeScore 0, a marker word placed after 70 distinct filler words gets no hit, and the same word placed first gets an `fts` leg. Repeats do not use up the cap: the marker after 80 repeats of two words is still found. A 6-token query keeps the stopword `the`, and a 71-token query drops it. Negative control: install the release before the cap into a scratch --tool-path and run the same copy and queries. There the paste takes tens of seconds, the stopword run times out, and both the trailing marker and the 71-token `the` are found (ADR-0126)
get_watch_status lists live registrations and their sync state

Watch a scratch directory (`settings ingest scope add`, `settings watch enable`, add_watch) holding x.md, w.md and y.md, plus node_modules/pkg/index.md and .git/notes.md, each with a term found nowhere else. Wait for three watch_files rows and leave node_modules readable (a `chmod 000` decoy is absent whether or not it is excluded, so that leg could never fail), wait 2 s, then edit y.md so watches.last_change_ts moves past x.md's watch_files.updated_at. Read both values while the server runs, because a stopped WAL bank will not open read-only. Stop the server. Replace one word of x.md with a new term of the same byte length and `touch -t $(date -r <t> +%Y%m%d%H%M.%S)` it, where t is between x.md's updated_at and last_change_ts. Rewrite w.md at a different size with a new term, and touch it to before its own updated_at. Restart on the same data root. Within seconds query finds both new terms, watch_files shows new updated_at and size for x.md and w.md, and get_watch_status reads Healthy. Neither the node_modules term nor the .git term is ever found. Premise: before the restart, updated_at(x.md) <= mtime(x.md) <= last_change_ts. A build without ADR-0121 finds neither new term, because it re-queues only files with mtime > last_change_ts. The 5-minute heal pass (WatchHostedService.HealInterval, event 322 at Debug) is optional: it needs a server left up for over 5 minutes (ADR-0121)
get_memories_sharing_ranking reports propose-tier candidates and queue state accurately
every tool in derived.mcp-tool-count and every prompt in derived.mcp-prompt-count is listed and reachable
emitted [LoggerMessage] event ids resolve against docs/reference/logging-event-ids.md

Shared watch publishes File rows to ordinary all-scope and shared all/shared queries; ordinary project-only has none; shared project-only and every ordinary-project-only tool refuse. Derive that set from declarations. Remove-watch retains content; re-add then delete-source removes mirrored document.

Exact reserved name mint refuses; lookup returns shared; SQLite projects remains empty before ordinary reader registration. Legacy registration under name shared prevents activation, CLI exits17, MCP shared-project-conflict, entries0.
Derive tool scope membership from declarations and compare with the live surface; every ordinary-project-only tool refuses the reserved shared target before side effects.

Every legacy tool name from the 2.0.0 rename map refuses as MCP isError with unknown-tool and exact replacement guidance. Compare current tools and prompts to derived facts; a raw JSON-RPC unknown-tool error is insufficient.

Seed distinguishable Memory/File/Code plus an unclassified control. Drive all seven nonempty entryType subsets and omitted default, including mixed case/spacing. Narrow sets return only declared selected types; default/all includes unclassified. Confirm kind_mask exactly 1..7. (2.1.0 changelog, ADR-0141)
Empty set, unknown vocabulary and all-comma input are refused; duplicates/interior empty tokens follow current parser contract. (EntryTypeParameter, 2.1.0 changelog)
get_entry requires one entryType, refuses missing/empty/composite/unknown; overlapping Memory/Code hash resolves chosen corpus; wrong taxonomy is unknown-hash without fallback. (2.1.0 changelog)

For each tested Memory, File and Code row, get_entry includes corpus matching the owning corpus (memory for Memory/File, code for Code); entryType remains corpus memory/code and entryKind states memory/file/code. (2.1.0 changelog)
Ingest a real document and add an agent note citing that same path. File mirror is File; note is Memory. Modify and re-ingest document; refreshed chunks remain File with no TTL. (2.1.0 changelog)
In full access mode set/clear Memory TTL; refuse setting and clearing File and Code-only hashes, and retain negative controls. (2.1.0 changelog, ADR-0148)

Seed age/rating and existing non-Memory TTLs, including an explicit historical File TTL, in a pre-v24 scratch bank. Include a project-scoped Memory row with age greater than its TTL and rating below the cleanup threshold, TTL-free Memory/File controls with age greater than that TTL and rating below the same threshold, and Code rows; use distinct hashes without shared counterparts. Verify migration to schema v24 clears all non-Memory TTLs and preserves Memory TTLs; subsequent File TTL writes are rejected. Run cleanup without dry run and verify it deletes the expired Memory row while preserving TTL-free Memory/File and all Code. (2.1.0 changelog, ADR-0148)

Drive isolated transcript/cloud merge where credentials allow: transcript chunks declare Memory and eligible TTL survives; File sync/rechunk does not introduce TTL. If unavailable record substituted focused sync test evidence explicitly. (2.1.0 changelog)

Upgrade real copied v19 and mixed-marker v20/v21 fixtures through installed package to current schema. Compare all durable IDs/embedding bytes, all prior search-quality columns, legacy mask mapping, explicit-kind preservation, integrity and product reopen. Disable watch registrations and external services in copies before serving. (2.1.0 changelog, ADR-0141)

Read both native ctx/type layouts and row-kind agreement; exercise typed vector-leg queries with bundled engine. Separately attach actual minority-type pretruncation oracle experiment for both modalities; never infer recall correctness merely from DDL. (ADR-0141)

Fresh/released upgraded bank rejects out-of-domain stored kind; doctor counts unclassified and unknown development-bank markers. Default queries can return these, narrower sets exclude them. (2.1.0 changelog)
Code-only lookup/query works against separate corpus without memory engine dependency or memory-engine warning. (2.1.0 changelog, ADR-0085)

Validate every decision tool's structuredContent against the outputSchema that tools/list advertises (jsonschema Draft 2020-12), the way Claude Code does, for record_decision, get_decision, query_decisions, find_decision_precedents, get_decision_graph and preview_decisions. Every reply must validate. A raw JSON-RPC client that reads only content[0].text cannot fail this item, so the other decision items do not cover it. (ADR-0142; MCP structured output)

register_decision_task then record_decision on a registered scratch project. A record without status is proposed, status=accepted is accepted, and an empty required field is refused as invalid-argument. Resending the same sessionId+requestId returns replayed=true with the same decisionId and revision; judge 'no duplicate' by the export counts, not by the replay flag alone. (ADR-0142, docs/how-to/record-project-decisions.md)

Each write guard must be seen refusing: amend with a stale expectedVersion -> decision-conflict naming currentVersion; accepted->proposed -> decision-invalid-transition; link_decisions with a stale expectedProjectRevision -> decision-conflict; amending a superseded decision -> decision-invalid-transition. Pair each refusal with the same call succeeding on fresh values. (ADR-0142, docs/how-to/record-project-decisions.md)

link_decisions depends_on appears in get_decision_graph with both nodes. query_decisions by literal text and by category return only the matching decision, and a no-match term returns [] (negative control). After supersede_decision, find_decision_precedents omits the superseded decision unless includeInactive=true. (ADR-0142, docs/how-to/record-project-decisions.md)

ai-raccoon decisions record/query/get --history/preview reach the same records through the server. export --all --output writes a file with mode 0600 on macOS and Linux, and permissions governed by the destination ACL on Windows, whose counts match what was written (decisions, versions, edges); a second export to the same path without --force exits 10. An unregistered project exits 18; a record file naming taskId exits 10 and sends nothing. (ADR-0142, docs/how-to/record-project-decisions.md)

settings access set <id> ro: record_decision over MCP returns access-denied, the CLI exits 17, projectRevision is unchanged and reads still work. After serve --restart on the same scratch port the project is still ro. Restore rw before any further write step. (ADR-0142, docs/how-to/record-project-decisions.md)

decisions import-semantica with tests/AiRaccoon.Tests/Resources/Semantica/export-graph-json-0.7.0.json: preview with the legacy tasks unregistered exits 17; a mapping with one decision's status removed exits 17 with a missing-status blocker; the clean preview exits 0 and prints the --apply command; apply creates decisions in their mapped statuses with replayed=false; re-running apply returns replayed=true and leaves the revision unchanged; export shows importRecords equal to entities+relationships. (ADR-0142, docs/how-to/record-project-decisions.md)

unlink_decisions with a stale expectedProjectRevision -> decision-conflict; with the current revision the edge leaves get_decision_graph but stays in export_decisions with removedAt and removalActor; unlinking a supersedes edge -> decision-invalid-transition (supersession is permanent). (ADR-0142, docs/how-to/record-project-decisions.md)

On a chain X1 depends_on X2 depends_on X3, get_decision_graph from X1 upstream: depth 0 = seed alone with truncated reason depth; depth 1 = 2 nodes, reason depth; depth 2 = 3 nodes, not truncated; maxNodes 2 = 2 nodes, reason nodes. downstream from X1 returns the seed alone (direction control). depth 11 and maxNodes 0 -> invalid-argument. Upstream = edges whose source is the node (DecisionService.Views.cs). (ADR-0142, docs/how-to/record-project-decisions.md)

Record enough decisions in one task to pass 1 MiB (reasoning is capped at 16 000 chars, so about 80 x 15 000). MCP export_decisions of that task -> decision-export-too-large naming the byte size and the CLI command; ai-raccoon decisions export of the same task exits 0 and its counts match what was recorded. (ADR-0142, docs/how-to/record-project-decisions.md)
Create a consistent backup before upgrade, validate SQLite integrity, preserve a durable copy and record its digest.
